walkthroughs.body_html:
Big businesses split work into departments:

  • Marketing — promotes products.
  • Finance — counts the money.
  • HR — looks after staff.
  • Operations — makes the product.

Front-line staff meet customers — shop floor, tills, call centre.

Back-office staff support them — payroll, IT, buying stock.

Both matter — no one works alone.

A business hierarchy is its layers:

  • Directors set the big plan.
  • Managers run teams.
  • Team members do the daily work.

Like a triangle: few at the top, many at the bottom. 🔺

mcqs.q: Why does a company's share price change?
options: Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness.
Share prices reflect investors' expectations about future profits — driven by company performance, sector trends, economic conditions, and market sentiment.
Share prices go up when a company makes more money this year.
Share prices are set by the government each morning.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness.
Just-in-time means delivering products to customers exactly on time.
Just-in-time means finishing work right before the deadline.
Holding minimal stock and receiving inputs only when needed for production — reducing storage costs but increasing vulnerability to supply disruption.

mcqs.q: What is Herzberg's distinction between hygiene factors and motivators?
options: Share prices are set by the government each morning.
Higher pay always motivates employees.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness.
Hygiene factors (pay, conditions, policies) prevent dissatisfaction when present but don't motivate; motivators (recognition, achievement, responsibility) create positive satisfaction.
